title: International English-Language News Headline Bias and Fallacy Dataset

methodology.scope: Three headlines per outlet, with a deliberately mixed set of topics including Ukraine/Russia, Gaza/Israel/Palestine, climate, migration, protests, elections, social justice and international affairs.
methodology.classification_note: The classifications are analytical judgments about headline wording and framing. They do not imply that the underlying article is false or that the outlet is intentionally misleading.

classification_levels.3: Moderate: a plausible classification, but reasonable disagreement is possible.
classification_levels.4: Strong: clear evaluative, emotional or selective framing.
classification_levels.5: Very strong: the rhetorical device or framing is unusually explicit.

headlines.title: Ukraine war: What would a ceasefire mean?
headlines.explanation: The wording moves immediately from whether a ceasefire is possible to its consequences, subtly making the ceasefire scenario the central frame.

headlines.title: Why are people risking their lives to cross the Channel?
headlines.explanation: The wording foregrounds danger and individual motivation rather than border policy, enforcement or aggregate migration statistics.

headlines.title: Climate change: How bad could things get?
headlines.explanation: The question directs attention toward negative outcomes and worst-case possibilities.

headlines.title: Putin has no incentive to end the war. Trump may have just given him one.
headlines.explanation: The headline asserts a particular internal motivation and then proposes a causal change in that motivation.

headlines.title: The slow burn of international outrage heats up over Israel's war in Gaza
headlines.explanation: The 'slow burn' and 'heats up' metaphor creates an escalating emotional narrative.

headlines.title: An increasing threat of mass starvation in Gaza, as pressure grows on Israel to let more aid in
headlines.explanation: The headline leads with the humanitarian consequence and then associates it with pressure on Israel. CNN's contemporaneous coverage described aid groups warning of spreading starvation.

headlines.title: Police and protesters scuffle as 110,000 join anti-migrant London protest
headlines.explanation: The confrontation is placed first even though the headline also reports the much larger participation figure. The original Reuters report describes the march as the culmination of a highly charged summer.

headlines.title: Pro-Palestinian protesters fight police in Milan, Italian ports blocked
headlines.explanation: The verbs 'fight' and 'blocked' foreground disruption and confrontation rather than the political claims motivating the protests.

headlines.title: UN agency warns displaced Gazans face floods, as emergency supplies blocked
headlines.explanation: The headline foregrounds vulnerable civilians and presents blocked supplies as the immediate contextual explanation for their exposure to flooding.

headlines.title: Putin Is Playing Trump. Will Trump Let Him?
headlines.explanation: A complex international conflict is converted into a two-person strategic game.

headlines.title: The Democrats Have a Problem. They Just Don't Know What It Is.
headlines.explanation: The headline treats a diverse political coalition as having a single problem and claims ignorance of that problem.

headlines.title: Protest at Minnesota Church Service Adds to Tensions Over ICE Tactics
headlines.explanation: The headline frames the church incident primarily as contributing to tensions surrounding ICE tactics rather than foregrounding the conduct that caused the controversy. Fox News subsequently criticized this framing, which makes it particularly useful for comparative analysis.

headlines.title: DCCC chair says $4 gas prices are Trump's broken promise amid Iran
headlines.explanation: The headline foregrounds a Democratic political attack and uses 'broken promise,' making the partisan dispute part of the frame.

headlines.title: Deputy AG warns US 'should be worried' about Minnesota after church disruption
headlines.explanation: The warning turns a local dispute into a national threat frame. The article reports the official's claim that the situation should concern Americans generally.

headlines.title: DHS slams New York Times' 'despicably misleading' headline after ICE shooting of violent illegal immigrant
headlines.explanation: Both 'despicably misleading' and 'violent illegal immigrant' are strongly evaluative constructions. The headline itself is also reporting one side's characterization of another outlet.

headlines.title: Israeli protesters stage 'day of disruption' calling for end to war in Gaza
headlines.explanation: The phrase 'day of disruption' foregrounds the disruptive tactics while the subheadline explains the political objective. The article reports tens of thousands participating and highways being blocked.

headlines.title: Wave of Earth Day protests as Americans mobilize against Trump
headlines.explanation: 'Wave' and 'mobilize against' construct a large-scale movement narrative and position Trump as the opposing actor.

headlines.title: 'Fossil fuel giants finally in the crosshairs': Cop30 avoids total failure
headlines.explanation: 'Giants,' 'crosshairs' and 'total failure' all communicate evaluation rather than simply describing the negotiations.

headlines.title: Why is the world letting Israel get away with Gaza?
headlines.explanation: The question presupposes both wrongdoing and collective international failure to respond.

headlines.title: Gaza: Is this the world's worst humanitarian crisis?
headlines.explanation: The superlative comparison encourages readers to evaluate Gaza against every other humanitarian crisis, even though such comparisons depend heavily on measurement criteria.

headlines.title: Why is the West losing its appetite for Ukraine?
headlines.explanation: 'The West' is treated as if it were a single actor possessing one psychological preference.

headlines.title: Trump's immigration crackdown is reshaping America
headlines.explanation: A complex policy process involving Congress, courts, agencies and states is organized around one individual.

headlines.title: Ukraine faces an uncertain future as U.S. support hangs in the balance
headlines.explanation: 'Hangs in the balance' dramatizes uncertainty and makes U.S. support the dominant explanatory variable.

headlines.title: Anti-Gaza war protests ramp up inside Israel as hunger is enveloping Gaza
headlines.explanation: The headline juxtaposes domestic Israeli protest with Palestinian suffering, encouraging the reader to interpret the protest through the humanitarian crisis. CNN used this framing in its July 2025 international broadcast.

headlines.title: Trump Deals Climate Blow by Exiting Crucial UN Bodies
headlines.explanation: 'Climate blow' tells the reader how to evaluate the policy rather than merely describing the withdrawal.

headlines.title: China's Economy Is Defying the Gloom
headlines.explanation: A complex economy is presented as an actor defying an opposing force, simplifying many indicators into a resilience narrative.

headlines.title: The Trump Trade Is Back
headlines.explanation: A broad collection of market movements is compressed into a political-personality label.

headlines.title: Trump keeps making threats. The world has stopped flinching.
headlines.explanation: 'The world' is treated as a unified actor with a common psychological response.

headlines.title: Putin is testing whether Trump really wants peace
headlines.explanation: The headline assigns a strategic intention to Putin and frames diplomacy primarily through the interaction of two personalities.

headlines.title: Democracy is on the ballot
headlines.explanation: The formulation can imply that one electoral outcome represents democracy while the alternative represents its negation.

headlines.title: Trump vows to inflict 'ECONOMIC D-DAY' on Iran
headlines.explanation: Capitalization and the D-Day comparison dramatically intensify the language around economic sanctions.

headlines.title: Putin has been playing games with peace talks
headlines.explanation: 'Playing games' implies insincerity or manipulation rather than simply describing negotiating behavior.

headlines.title: Migration crisis: Why Britain can't cope
headlines.explanation: 'Crisis' and 'can't cope' establish two conclusions before the explanatory question begins.

headlines.title: Climate activist Greta Thunberg joins aid ship sailing to Gaza aimed at breaking Israel's blockade
headlines.explanation: The celebrity/activist identity provides a highly salient entry point into a geopolitical humanitarian story. AP's article describes Thunberg and other activists aboard the Madleen.

headlines.title: Protesters clash with police
headlines.explanation: The conflict itself becomes the defining feature of the protest, potentially obscuring the political demands and peaceful participation.

headlines.title: Immigrants from Central Asia find hostility and violence in Russia
headlines.explanation: The headline centers migrants' experience of hostility and violence rather than Russian immigration policy or security concerns.

headlines.title: Europe faces a moment of truth over Ukraine
headlines.explanation: 'Moment of truth' implies a decisive binary choice and compresses a long-running policy debate into a single dramatic juncture.

headlines.title: The green backlash is here
headlines.explanation: A variety of political and economic developments are presented as one coherent 'backlash'.

headlines.title: Scott Bessent: an economic D-Day is coming for Iran
headlines.explanation: A senior official's dramatic analogy becomes the organizing concept of the headline.

headlines.title: 5-year-old asylum seeker detained as ICE expands enforcement in Minnesota
headlines.explanation: The very young age of the subject produces strong emotional salience and makes the immigration-policy story concrete. Fox News subsequently reported that DHS disputed the characterization, making this a particularly useful example for examining disputed framing.

headlines.title: Trump administration reveals list of civil rights, climate change materials removed from national parks
headlines.explanation: The headline groups civil-rights and climate materials together, encouraging the reader to interpret the removals as part of one broader political project.

headlines.title: Climate change is coming for your wallet
headlines.explanation: The headline translates a systemic environmental issue into a direct threat to the reader's personal finances.

headlines.title: Trump's EPA revokes the 'endangerment finding' on greenhouse gases, a major reversal in climate policy
headlines.explanation: 'Major reversal' supplies an evaluative characterization of the policy change.

headlines.title: Russia's war in Ukraine enters a dangerous new phase
headlines.explanation: 'Dangerous new phase' is a predictive and emotionally charged characterization rather than a purely descriptive one.

headlines.title: U.S. carries out more strikes as Trump threatens Iran
headlines.explanation: The juxtaposition connects military action and presidential rhetoric, encouraging a narrative of continuing escalation.

headlines.title: Oil prices surge after Donald Trump says Iran will 'get a beating'
headlines.explanation: The headline places the price movement immediately after Trump's threat, inviting a causal interpretation while using highly aggressive language.

headlines.title: China's economy is on the brink. Here's what it means for the world
headlines.explanation: 'On the brink' dramatizes economic weakness and encourages readers to focus on potentially severe downstream consequences.

headlines.title: The clean-energy revolution is running out of steam
headlines.explanation: The metaphor turns a complex collection of investment, technology and policy indicators into a single narrative of acceleration or decline.

headlines.title: Ukraine: Can Europe stop Putin?
headlines.explanation: The conflict is simplified into Europe versus one individual, minimizing the roles of Russia's state apparatus, Ukraine and other actors.

headlines.title: Europe's migration problem: Can the EU find a solution?
headlines.explanation: Calling migration a 'problem' establishes a normative frame before discussing what the underlying problem actually is.

headlines.title: What's behind the Iran regime's 'revenge propaganda'?
headlines.explanation: Calling the communication 'propaganda' is itself an interpretive conclusion. The quotation marks partly signal that the term is contested.

headlines.title: Ukraine war: Is Putin finally ready for peace?
headlines.explanation: The headline makes Putin's presumed internal willingness the key explanatory variable.

headlines.title: Gaza: How did the world let this happen?
headlines.explanation: The question presupposes collective international responsibility for the outcome.

headlines.title: Europe turns right: What does it mean?
headlines.explanation: Election results from many countries are compressed into a single continent-wide ideological movement.

headlines.title: Europe's migration crisis: Is the EU losing control?
headlines.explanation: 'Crisis' and 'losing control' establish a threat narrative before the reader encounters the evidence.

headlines.title: Europe's climate ambitions collide with political reality
headlines.explanation: The wording sets climate ambition against 'political reality', implicitly positioning one as aspirational and the other as constraining.

headlines.title: Europe's far right is surging. Here's why
headlines.explanation: 'Surging' implies rapid and substantial growth and encourages the reader to see separate electoral developments as one coherent movement.

headlines.title: Ukraine seeks peace as Russia presses its offensive
headlines.explanation: The parallel verbs assign Ukraine the role of seeker and Russia the role of aggressor, producing a strong asymmetry of agency.

headlines.title: Migrants face uncertain future as U.S. tightens border
headlines.explanation: The migrants' vulnerability is placed before the policy rationale or security argument.

headlines.title: Democracy under threat around the world
headlines.explanation: A broad global claim treats diverse political situations as manifestations of one common threat.

headlines.title: The climate emergency is getting worse - and politicians are failing us
headlines.explanation: 'Emergency' and 'failing us' combine threat language with an explicit judgment about political responsibility.

headlines.title: How the world failed Gaza
headlines.explanation: 'The world' is treated as a collective actor and 'failed' assigns a broad moral judgment.

headlines.title: Britain is broken. Can it be fixed?
headlines.explanation: 'Broken' is an extremely broad evaluative characterization that converts many separate social and economic problems into a single diagnosis.
